study.title: His loving devotion endures forever
study.intro: Psalm 136 is a great responsive song of thanksgiving. Every one of its twenty-six verses ends with the same refrain: 'His loving devotion endures forever.' One voice names a reason to give thanks, from creation to the exodus to daily bread, and the congregation answers each time with the refrain. By the end, the whole story of God's dealings with His people has been told as one long story of steadfast love.
study.context: Jewish tradition calls Psalm 136 the 'Great Hallel' and sings it at Passover. Its refrain appears elsewhere in worship: when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 16:34), at the temple's dedication (2 Chronicles 7:3), before Jehoshaphat's battle (2 Chronicles 20:21) and when the second temple's foundation was laid (Ezra 3:11). It follows the outline of Psalm 135: creation, exodus, conquest, inheritance.
study.peopleNote: No author is named. The psalm retells events involving Israel, Pharaoh, Sihon and Og, and the leaders God used, such as Moses. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Give thanks, He is good
verses.heading: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good
verses.meaning: 'Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good. His loving devotion endures forever.' The song starts with the simplest truth of all: God is good, so thank Him. Then comes the refrain that will be repeated twenty-six times. God's loving devotion, His loyal, covenant love, never runs out. Every story in this psalm will show that same love from a different angle.
verses.context: This opening line appears at key moments in Israel's worship, such as 1 Chronicles 16:34 and Ezra 3:11. Jeremiah 33:11 prophesied this song would be heard again in restored Jerusalem. Jesus and His disciples likely sang Passover psalms before going to the Mount of Olives (Matthew 26:30).
explore: Loving devotion
The Hebrew hesed: God's steadfast, loyal, covenant love that never gives up on His people.
Refrain
A line repeated after each verse of a song, often sung by the whole congregation.
verses.reflect: Try saying 'His loving devotion endures forever' after each thing you are thankful for today.
verses.alt: A large congregation in a courtyard singing with raised faces at morning.

verses.title: The God of gods
verses.heading: Give thanks to the God of gods
verses.meaning: 'Give thanks to the God of gods. His loving devotion endures forever.' The LORD is above every other power people call 'god.' The title means the supreme God, the One over all. Yet this highest God is not cold or distant. His defining quality is loving devotion that never ends. Greatness and love are joined together in Him.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 10:17 calls the LORD the God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty and awesome God who shows no partiality. Daniel 2:47 records a king confessing that Daniel's God is the God of gods.
explore: God of gods
A Hebrew way of saying the supreme God, greater than every other so-called god.
Supreme
Highest in rank and authority, with no one above or equal.
verses.reflect: How does knowing the highest God is also the most loving God affect your prayers?
verses.alt: Sunlight streaming over a mountain range above the clouds.

verses.title: The Lord of lords
verses.heading: Give thanks to the Lord of lords
verses.meaning: 'Give thanks to the Lord of lords. His loving devotion endures forever.' He is master over every master, ruler over every ruler. No king, government or boss has the final word; God does. The New Testament gives this same title to Jesus, the Lamb who conquers. And the One with all authority uses it with steadfast love.
verses.context: Revelation 17:14 says the Lamb will conquer because He is Lord of lords and King of kings. 1 Timothy 6:15 calls God the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
explore: Lord of lords
Master over all other masters, the ruler with ultimate authority.
Authority
The right and power to rule, give commands and make final decisions.
verses.reflect: What authority in your life do you need to see as under the Lord of lords?
verses.alt: An empty royal hall with banners and light pouring through high windows.

verses.title: He alone does wonders
verses.heading: He alone does great wonders
verses.meaning: 'He alone does great wonders. His loving devotion endures forever.' The psalm now begins listing what God has done. First, a summary: only He does great wonders. No one else can create, rescue and sustain as He does. And every wonder flows from His loving devotion. His miracles are not shows of power for their own sake; they are acts of love.
verses.context: Psalm 72:18 says the God of Israel alone does wondrous things. Exodus 15:11 asks who is like the LORD, awesome in praises, working wonders. Jesus' miracles were signs of God's kingdom and compassion (Matthew 14:14).
explore: Wonders
Astonishing acts that cause awe because only God could do them.
Alone
Only, without anyone else's help or anyone able to do the same.
verses.reflect: What wonder has God done that you can thank Him for?
verses.alt: A starry night sky over a quiet desert landscape.

verses.title: Heavens by His insight
verses.heading: By His insight He made the heavens
verses.meaning: 'By His insight He made the heavens. His loving devotion endures forever.' Creation begins the story. God made the sky and everything in it with wisdom and understanding. The universe is not an accident but a work of brilliant design. And even creation is an act of love: God made a world where He could share His goodness with those He would create.
verses.context: Proverbs 3:19 says the LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding. Jeremiah 10:12 says He stretched out the heavens by His understanding. Genesis 1:1 opens the story of creation.
explore: Insight
Understanding and skill; deep wisdom used to make something well.
Heavens
The sky above and everything in it: clouds, sun, moon and stars.
verses.reflect: Look up at the sky today. What does it tell you about God's wisdom and love?
verses.alt: A vast blue sky with soft clouds over gentle hills.

verses.title: Earth over the waters
verses.heading: He spread out the earth
verses.meaning: 'He spread out the earth upon the waters. His loving devotion endures forever.' God shaped dry land and set it in place among the waters, making a home where life could flourish. The ancient world feared the sea as chaos, but God put it in its place. The ground you walk on is a gift of His love, prepared so people could live.
verses.context: Genesis 1:9-10 tells of God gathering the waters and making dry land appear. Psalm 24:2 says He founded the earth upon the seas. Isaiah 42:5 says He spread out the earth and gives breath to its people.
explore: Spread out
Stretched or laid out flat, like hammering metal thin or laying out a rug.
Waters
The seas and deep waters, often pictured in the ancient world as chaos God controls.
verses.reflect: How is the ground under your feet, and the home it provides, a sign of God's love?
verses.alt: Green coastline meeting a calm sea at sunrise.

verses.title: The great lights
verses.heading: He made the great lights
verses.meaning: 'He made the great lights—His loving devotion endures forever.' Next God made the sun, moon and stars. Many nations worshiped these lights as gods. Here they are simply things God made, lamps hung in the sky for people's good. The sun that warms the earth and the moon that guides the night are gifts of His steadfast love.
verses.context: Genesis 1:14-16 describes God making the great lights for signs, seasons, days and years. Deuteronomy 4:19 warns Israel not to worship the sun, moon and stars. James 1:17 calls God the Father of lights.
explore: Great lights
The sun and moon, the largest lights in the sky, made by God.
Seasons
Regular times of the year marked by the sun and moon, such as feasts and harvests.
verses.reflect: What everyday gift, like light or warmth, can you thank God for today?
verses.alt: Golden sunlight and a pale moon both visible over a field at dusk.

verses.title: Sun for the day
verses.heading: The sun to rule the day
verses.meaning: 'the sun to rule the day, His loving devotion endures forever.' God gave the sun a job: to rule the day, giving light, warmth and growth. It does not rule as a god; it serves as a servant. Every sunrise is a quiet reminder that God's faithful love keeps showing up, day after day, without fail, just as the sun does.
verses.context: Genesis 1:16 says the greater light rules the day. Matthew 5:45 says God makes His sun rise on the evil and the good. Lamentations 3:23 says His mercies are new every morning.
explore: Rule
To govern or be in charge of; here the sun's role in marking and lighting the day.
Sunrise
The daily appearing of the sun, a sign of God's faithfulness to creation.
verses.reflect: Tomorrow at sunrise, how might you remember God's love that is new every morning?
verses.alt: The sun rising over a valley with long morning shadows.

verses.title: Moon and stars for the night
verses.heading: The moon and stars to govern the night
verses.meaning: 'the moon and stars to govern the night. His loving devotion endures forever.' Even darkness has light. God placed the moon and stars to give guidance in the night, helping travelers find their way and marking months and seasons. When life feels like night, God has not left us in total darkness; His love still shines.
verses.context: Genesis 1:16 says the lesser light rules the night, along with the stars. Psalm 8:3 marvels at the moon and stars God set in place. Isaiah 40:26 says God calls each star by name.
explore: Govern
To guide and rule over; the moon and stars give order to the night.
Stars
Distant lights in the night sky that God created and calls by name.
verses.reflect: In what 'night' season do you need to remember God's light still shines?
verses.alt: A full moon and bright stars above tents in a quiet desert camp.

verses.title: Firstborn struck down
verses.heading: He struck down the firstborn of Egypt
verses.meaning: 'He struck down the firstborn of Egypt His loving devotion endures forever.' The psalm moves from creation to redemption. The final plague was a terrible judgment on Egypt, yet the refrain still follows: His loving devotion endures forever. God's love for His enslaved people meant acting against the oppressor who refused to let them go.
verses.context: Exodus 12:29-32 tells of the final plague and Pharaoh's release of Israel. Exodus 4:22-23 calls Israel God's firstborn son, whom Pharaoh refused to release. God's judgment and love work together for His people's freedom.
explore: Firstborn
The eldest son, honored as heir; Egypt's firstborn died in the tenth plague.
Oppressor
Someone who uses power to crush and enslave others unjustly.
verses.reflect: How does God's willingness to act against oppression show His love?
verses.alt: A darkened Egyptian city at midnight under a sliver of moon.

verses.title: Brought out from Egypt
verses.heading: Brought Israel out from among them
verses.meaning: 'and brought Israel out from among them His loving devotion endures forever.' After centuries of slavery, God led His people out. They left not as escaped fugitives but as a freed nation. The exodus is the Old Testament's great picture of salvation: God taking His people out of bondage. Christians see in it a picture of being freed from sin through Jesus.
verses.context: Exodus 12:41 says all the LORD's divisions went out of Egypt. Exodus 20:2 opens the Ten Commandments with 'I am the LORD who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.' Colossians 1:13 says God rescued us from darkness.
explore: Exodus
The going out of Israel from Egypt, God's great act of rescue from slavery.
Bondage
Slavery or captivity, being held under someone else's control.
verses.reflect: What has God brought you out of? Thank Him for that rescue.
verses.alt: A long column of families with animals leaving a city at dawn.

verses.title: A mighty hand
verses.heading: An outstretched arm
verses.meaning: 'with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. His loving devotion endures forever.' God's rescue was powerful. A mighty hand and outstretched arm picture a strong warrior reaching out to fight and to save. These images describe God's power, not a human body. No one could stop Him when He moved to free His people.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 26:8 says the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Jeremiah 32:17 says nothing is too hard for the God who made the heavens with His outstretched arm. Isaiah 59:1 says His arm is not too short to save.
explore: Mighty hand
A picture of God's great power to act and accomplish what He wills.
Outstretched arm
A picture of God reaching out in strength to fight for and rescue His people.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God's mighty power to reach into your life?
verses.alt: A strong wind bending reeds along a marshy shore.

verses.title: The sea divided
verses.heading: He divided the Red Sea in two
verses.meaning: 'He divided the Red Sea in two His loving devotion endures forever.' Trapped between the sea and Pharaoh's army, Israel had no way out. Then God split the waters. What seemed impossible became a path. This is the story believers have told for thousands of years: when there is no way, God can make one.
verses.context: Exodus 14:21 says the LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night and made the sea dry land. Isaiah 43:16 calls God the one who makes a way in the sea and a path through mighty waters.
explore: Red Sea
The body of water Israel crossed on dry ground when leaving Egypt.
Divided
Split apart; God parted the waters so they stood like walls on either side.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God to make a way where there seems to be no way?
verses.alt: Walls of seawater on either side of a dry seabed path.

verses.title: Through the midst
verses.heading: Led Israel through the midst
verses.meaning: 'and led Israel through the midst, His loving devotion endures forever.' God did not just open the sea; He led His people through it. They walked step by step between walls of water, trusting Him. Faith often means walking through the middle of something frightening, with God leading. His love does not only make a way; it walks us through it.
verses.context: Exodus 14:22 says Israel went through the sea on dry ground with the water as a wall on their right and left. Hebrews 11:29 says by faith they passed through the Red Sea. Isaiah 43:2 says when you pass through the waters, I will be with you.
explore: Midst
The middle or center of something; here walking right through the sea.
Led
Guided and went before; God led His people every step of the way.
verses.reflect: What frightening 'middle' are you walking through? How is God leading you?
verses.alt: Families walking on a dry path between towering waves at night.

verses.title: Pharaoh's army swept away
verses.heading: Swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea
verses.meaning: 'but swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea. His loving devotion endures forever.' The same waters that saved Israel overwhelmed the army chasing them. The oppressor who refused to let God's people go was finally defeated. God's love for His people meant the end of the power that enslaved them. What once terrified them would never threaten them again.
verses.context: Exodus 14:27-28 says the waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen. Exodus 15:1-21 records Moses' and Miriam's songs of victory. Exodus 14:13 says, 'The Egyptians you see today you will never see again.'
explore: Pharaoh
The title of Egypt's king; this Pharaoh refused to release Israel from slavery.
Swept
Carried away violently, as by a flood or rushing water.
verses.reflect: What old enemy or fear has God already defeated in your life?
verses.alt: Waves crashing back over a seabed with broken chariot wheels on the shore.

verses.title: Through the wilderness
verses.heading: He led His people through the wilderness
verses.meaning: 'He led His people through the wilderness. His loving devotion endures forever.' After the sea came forty years in the desert. God did not abandon them there. He gave manna, water from the rock, a pillar of cloud and fire. The wilderness was hard, but His love led them every day. Seasons of wandering are also seasons of His faithful care.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 8:2-4 says God led Israel forty years in the wilderness, fed them with manna and their clothes did not wear out. Exodus 13:21 describes the pillar of cloud and fire. Isaiah 63:13 speaks of God leading them through the depths.
explore: Wilderness
The desert between Egypt and Canaan where Israel wandered for forty years.
Manna
Bread-like food God sent from heaven each morning to feed Israel in the desert.
verses.reflect: What wilderness have you walked through where God still provided?
verses.alt: A pillar of cloud over a desert camp of tents at dawn.

verses.title: Great kings fall
verses.heading: He struck down great kings
verses.meaning: 'He struck down great kings His loving devotion endures forever.' On the way to the promised land, powerful kings stood in Israel's path. God defeated them. No ruler, however great, could block God's promise. When we face powers that seem unbeatable, this verse reminds us that God's love is stronger than any opposition.
verses.context: Numbers 21 describes the defeat of kings who refused Israel passage. Joshua 12 lists thirty-one kings defeated. Psalm 2:2-4 says the kings of the earth set themselves against the LORD, but He laughs at their plans.
explore: Great kings
Powerful rulers with large territories, fortified cities and armies.
Struck down
Defeated completely so they could no longer stand in the way.
verses.reflect: What 'great' power seems to stand in your way? How does God's love speak to it?
verses.alt: A walled city gate standing open and abandoned on a hilltop.

verses.title: Mighty kings slain
verses.heading: And slaughtered mighty kings
verses.meaning: 'and slaughtered mighty kings—His loving devotion endures forever.' The line repeats with emphasis. These kings were mighty, famous for their strength. Yet they could not stand against the LORD. This is not a celebration of violence for its own sake but a testimony that God keeps His promises even against the strongest resistance.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 7:24 promised God would give kings into Israel's hand. Joshua 21:45 says not one of the LORD's good promises failed. Psalm 135:10 recalls the same victories.
explore: Mighty
Strong and powerful, often used of warriors and kings.
Testimony
A witness to what God has done, told so others will trust Him.
verses.reflect: What promise of God are you trusting Him to keep despite strong resistance?
verses.alt: Broken spears and shields lying in tall grass on a hillside.

verses.title: Sihon of the Amorites
verses.heading: Sihon king of the Amorites
verses.meaning: 'Sihon king of the Amorites His loving devotion endures forever.' Sihon refused to let Israel pass peacefully and attacked them instead. God gave Israel the victory. His defeat became a story that spread to other nations and gave courage to Israel. Even a single named victory is worth thanking God for, because each one shows His steadfast love in action.
verses.context: Numbers 21:21-24 tells how Sihon refused Israel passage, came out to fight and was defeated. Deuteronomy 2:30-33 describes the battle. Joshua 2:10 shows the story struck fear into Jericho.
explore: Sihon
An Amorite king east of the Jordan who attacked Israel and was defeated.
Amorites
A Canaanite people group living in the hill country and east of the Jordan.
verses.reflect: What specific moment of God's help can you name and thank Him for?
verses.alt: A dusty road winding through Amorite hill country with stone towers.

verses.title: Og of Bashan
verses.heading: Og king of Bashan
verses.meaning: 'and Og king of Bashan—His loving devotion endures forever.' Og ruled the rich land of Bashan and was remembered as one of the last of the giants. To human eyes he seemed impossible to defeat. Yet God told Moses not to fear him, and Israel won. The giants in our lives are no match for the love of God.
verses.context: Numbers 21:33-35 records God telling Moses, 'Do not fear him,' before the battle with Og. Deuteronomy 3:11 describes Og's iron bed over thirteen feet long. Deuteronomy 31:8 says the LORD goes before you; do not be afraid.
explore: Og
King of Bashan, remembered as one of the last of the giant Rephaim.
Bashan
A fertile highland region east of the Sea of Galilee, known for strong cattle and oaks.
verses.reflect: What 'giant' do you need to hear God say 'Do not fear it' about?
verses.alt: Oak forests and lush pastures of Bashan under bright sky.

verses.title: Land given as inheritance
verses.heading: He gave their land as an inheritance
verses.meaning: 'and He gave their land as an inheritance, His loving devotion endures forever.' The victories led to a gift. God gave land as an inheritance, a home passed down within families. Israel did not build this home by their own power. They received it. Every good place God gives us to live, work and belong is a gift of His love.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 6:10-11 reminds Israel they would live in cities they did not build and eat from vineyards they did not plant. Joshua 24:13 repeats this. Acts 17:26 says God determines the boundaries of where people live.
explore: Inheritance
Property passed down as a family's portion, received as a gift.
Home
A settled place to live and belong, given by God to His people.
verses.reflect: What home or place of belonging has God given you? Thank Him for it.
verses.alt: A farmhouse among vineyards and olive groves in afternoon light.

verses.title: A heritage for His servant
verses.heading: A heritage to His servant Israel
verses.meaning: 'a heritage to His servant Israel. His loving devotion endures forever.' The land was given to Israel, called God's servant. That title is an honor: Israel was chosen to serve God's purposes in the world. Their heritage came with a calling. God's gifts to us are never just for our comfort; they equip us to serve Him and bless others.
verses.context: Isaiah 41:8 calls Israel 'My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen.' Isaiah 49:6 says God's servant would be a light to the nations. 1 Peter 4:10 says each should use whatever gift he has received to serve others.
explore: Heritage
Something valuable passed down to belong to a family over generations.
Servant
One who serves another; Israel was called God's servant to carry out His purposes.
verses.reflect: How can the gifts God has given you be used to serve others?
verses.alt: A shepherd leading a flock across family pastureland at morning.

verses.title: Remembered in our low estate
verses.heading: He remembered us in our low estate
verses.meaning: 'He remembered us in our low estate His loving devotion endures forever.' Now the psalm becomes personal: 'us.' When God's people were brought low, through defeat, exile or failure, He remembered them. To be remembered by God means He acts on your behalf. No matter how low you sink, His steadfast love does not forget you.
verses.context: Mary sang that God had looked on the humble estate of His servant (Luke 1:48). Exodus 2:24-25 says God heard Israel's groaning and remembered His covenant. Isaiah 49:15 says even if a mother forgets her child, God will not forget you.
explore: Low estate
A humble, weak or humiliated condition, being brought down.
Remembered
Called to mind and acted upon; God's remembering always leads to help.
verses.reflect: When have you felt low, and how did God remember you?
verses.alt: A lone figure sitting on a riverbank as dawn begins to break.

verses.title: Freed from enemies
verses.heading: And freed us from our enemies
verses.meaning: 'and freed us from our enemies. His loving devotion endures forever.' God did not only remember; He rescued. The word 'freed' can mean to snatch away or tear loose. God pulled His people out of the grip of those who oppressed them. Whatever holds you, His love is strong enough to break that grip and set you free.
verses.context: Judges 2:16-18 tells of God raising judges to save Israel from enemies. Luke 1:74 speaks of being rescued from the hand of our enemies to serve God without fear. John 8:36 says if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
explore: Freed
Rescued, snatched away or torn loose from someone's grip.
Enemies
Those who actively oppose and seek to harm God's people and purposes.
verses.reflect: What is holding you that you can ask God to free you from?
verses.alt: A bird flying free over a broken fence into open countryside.

verses.title: Food for every creature
verses.heading: He gives food to every creature
verses.meaning: 'He gives food to every creature. His loving devotion endures forever.' The psalm widens to include all living things. God's love is not limited to big rescues; it shows up in daily bread for people and animals alike. Every meal you eat and every bird that finds seed is a sign of His ongoing care. His love sustains the whole world.
verses.context: Psalm 104:27-28 says all creatures look to God to give them food in due season. Psalm 145:15 says the eyes of all look to Him. Jesus taught that God feeds the birds of the air (Matthew 6:26) and to pray for daily bread.
explore: Creature
Any living being God has made, people and animals alike.
Provision
Supplying what is needed, especially food and care for daily life.
verses.reflect: Before your next meal, how might you thank God for His daily love?
verses.alt: Birds pecking seed in a field while a family shares bread nearby.

verses.title: The God of heaven
verses.heading: Give thanks to the God of heaven
verses.meaning: 'Give thanks to the God of heaven! His loving devotion endures forever.' The psalm ends where it began: with thanks. God is the God of heaven, ruling over all from above. After telling the whole story, from creation to daily bread, the conclusion is the same. Every part of life is wrapped in His love that endures forever. Gratitude is the right response to all of it.
verses.context: The title 'God of heaven' is common in Ezra and Nehemiah after the exile (Nehemiah 1:4). 1 Thessalonians 5:18 says to give thanks in all circumstances. Psalm 118:29 ends with the same call to give thanks for His enduring love.
explore: God of heaven
A title for God as the supreme ruler over all, used often after the exile.
Endures forever
Continues without end; God's love never runs out or stops.
verses.reflect: Write your own short list of reasons to thank God, ending each with 'His love endures forever.'
verses.alt: A starry sky stretching over hills with a small village below.
